features.title: Trend weight EWMA over irregular gaps
steps: Add a trend-weight calculation to StezuCore. Input: dated weigh-ins on irregular days. Output: the trend on each weigh-in day.
The first weigh-in seeds the trend. For a gap of d days the new weigh-in gets weight 1 - (1 - alpha)^d, with alpha configurable (default 0.1 per day).
Days without a weigh-in are absent, not zero, and do not update the trend.
Return a confidence with the trend, based on how many weigh-ins it rests on and how recent they are.

features.title: Expenditure estimate
steps: Add an expenditure estimate: mean logged intake over the last 21 days minus (trend change over those days x 3500 kcal/lb) / 21.
Exclude partial days: logged intake under 50% of that week's typical (median) intake.
Return insufficient data, never 0, when the window lacks intake or trend data.
Return a confidence with the estimate.

features.title: Weekly calorie target rule
steps: Add the weekly target rule from SPEC.md with all thresholds configurable.
Return insufficient data and no change with fewer than 4 weigh-ins in the week or fewer than 21 days of data.
Raise the target by the configured step (100 to 150 kcal) when the 3-week trend rate is more than 0.15 lb/week under the target rate; lower it by 100 kcal when it is more than 0.25 lb/week over.
Allow at most one change per week, and return the reason and a confidence with every result.

features.title: Protein floor flag
steps: Add a protein floor check over a 3-day rolling mean of daily protein.
Use the low end of each meal's estimate range.
The floor is a configurable parameter; tests use synthetic values.
With fewer than 3 days of logged food return insufficient data, not a flag.

features.title: Home screen three cards from a view model
steps: Add a HomeViewModel that produces the Data, Food and Workout cards (label, subtitle, value text) from core values.
Time of day picks the inverted card; inject the clock.
Missing values render as --, never 0.
HomeView renders the view model's cards with the DESIGN.md tokens.

features.title: HealthKit body-mass read behind the HealthStore protocol
steps: Define a HealthStore protocol in StezuCore with an async read of body-mass samples, plus a FakeHealthStore for tests.
Implement the protocol in the app with HealthKit, read-only body mass. Needs approval: HealthKit entitlement and capability.
Denied authorization or no samples is absent data, not zero.

features.title: One-tap weigh-in write
steps: Add a body-mass write to the HealthStore protocol; the fake records writes.
The weigh-in control is prefilled from the last weigh-in and adjusted without a keyboard; one tap writes the sample.
Needs approval: HealthKit write access.

features.title: Workout session model with last-session numbers and a rest timer
steps: Add a workout session model: exercises, sets (weight and reps) and a one-call log-set operation.
Expose the last session's numbers for each exercise; absent when there is no previous session.
Add a rest timer driven by an injected clock.

features.title: Double-progression rule
steps: Add a double-progression suggestion: add reps within the rep range, then add weight once every set reaches the top of the range.
Rep range and weight step are configurable.
No suggestion without a last session (absent, not zero).

features.title: Dining menu models and client against a VM endpoint
steps: Add Codable models for dining menus (FoodPro) as served by a VM endpoint.
Add a client that takes an injected transport protocol, so core needs no networking import and tests need no network.
Use a synthetic fixture. An unavailable menu is absent, not an empty menu.
Needs approval: the endpoint URL and token handling.

features.title: Tap a Home card to open its area, then move between areas with the three bottom circles
steps: Launch the app. Home shows three tall cards, Data, Food and Workout, each with a label, a subtitle and a number ("--" when there is no data).
Tap the Workout card. The Workout screen opens with the bottom nav: three 58 pt circles (Data, Food, Workout), Workout black, as in DESIGN.md.
Tap the Food circle. The Food screen opens and the Food circle is black. Tap the Data circle. The Data screen opens and the Data circle is black.
Tap the Home button at the top left. Home shows again.
Keep the ids the smoke test uses: home.card.<area>, screen.<area>.title and nav.home. Add nav.circle.<area> for the circles.
features.tap_budget: 1 tap from Home into any area; 1 tap between areas; 1 tap back Home

features.title: Set the server address and token once in Settings
steps: On Home, tap the gear. Settings shows Server address and Token, empty on first launch.
Type an address and a token (the keyboard is fine here) and tap Save. The token goes to the Keychain and shows masked; the address goes to app settings. Neither is ever committed.
Tap Test connection. The app calls the server through the VM client with the bearer token and shows Connected (in -uitest the fake transport answers GET /health).

The live app now uses a URLSession transport built from these settings instead of UnconfiguredVMTransport. With no server set, every server feature shows "Set up the server in Settings", never a crash or a 0.
features.tap_budget: 1 tap from Home to Settings; typing only on this screen

features.title: Tap Workout, see the five generic templates, and start Day 1
steps: Tap the Workout card. The black card is the next template in the rotation (Day 1 on first launch) with its exercises; below it, a row for each other template and Empty workout. This week's sessions and working sets show "--".

The templates come from a bundled generic seed, PrebuiltWorkouts.json with a seedVersion: a generic 5-day split, never Isaac's program (D-034). On launch a newer seed is upserted by key; templates the user edited and all history are left alone.
Tap Start. The logger opens on the first exercise: its name, "Set 1 of N" and the template's rep range.

features.title: Log a prefilled set in one tap, adjust it with steppers, and undo it
steps: Start Day 1. The big black Log card shows the current set prefilled with weight and reps.
Tap Log. The set appears as logged and the card moves to "Set 2 of N" with the same numbers. The set is saved to the store at that moment.
Tap + on weight (the exercise's step, default 5 lb) and - on reps. No keyboard appears. Tap Log: the new numbers are logged.
Tap the bodyweight toggle: weight shows "BW" and is stored as nil, never 0.
Tap Undo. The last set disappears and the Log card returns to it.
features.tap_budget: 1 tap to log a set; 1 tap to undo; 1 tap per stepper step

features.title: See last session's numbers beside each set, from the same template first
steps: Launch with -uitest-scenario workout-history: synthetic past sessions where Day 1 and Day 2 share an exercise.

Start Day 1. Each set row shows the last numbers and their age ("Last 60 x 8, 7d ago" style) from the last Day 1 session, not the newer Day 2 one. With no session of this template, any template's last session is used.
The Log card is prefilled from those numbers.
An exercise never done before shows "--" and the Log card stays disabled until a weight is set or bodyweight is chosen.

features.title: After logging a set, rest counts down by itself, with +15, -15, Skip and a lock-screen Live Activity
steps: Log a set. A rest countdown starts at the template's rest for that exercise, with no tap.
Tap +15 s, then -15 s: the countdown changes and the start time is kept. Tap Skip: the countdown goes away.

While it runs, the app starts the RestActivity Live Activity (App/Shared/RestActivityAttributes) and updates and ends it with the countdown, and schedules a local notification for zero. Both sit behind a protocol with a fake in -uitest.
Check on the phone that the widget extension installs with a free account (D-033); note the result in PROGRESS.md.
features.tap_budget: 0 taps to start a rest; 1 tap to adjust or skip

features.title: Swap an exercise from the library, or add a custom one
steps: In the logger, tap the exercise's menu, then Swap. The Exercises library opens: a search field, a list grouped by muscle, each row with when it was last done ("--" if never).
Type part of a name: the list filters. Tap an exercise: the logger shows it in place of the old one for this session only; the template is unchanged.
Tap New exercise, enter name, equipment, muscle and rest (the only keyboard in Workout) and Save. It appears marked custom with a stable key and can be picked.
features.tap_budget: 2 taps to swap (menu, pick); about 4 taps plus typing for a custom exercise

features.title: Tap Finish to save the workout and write it to Apple Health
steps: Log at least one set and tap Finish (no confirmation). The logger closes; the Workout screen shows this week's sessions and working sets.

The session is written through HealthStore.saveStrengthWorkout(start:end:externalID:) as a traditional strength training HKWorkout built with HKWorkoutBuilder, with no energy samples. The external id makes a retry safe. The session row shows "In Health" (the fake HealthStore records the write in -uitest).
If the write is denied or fails, the session still saves and shows "Not in Health".
Finishing with no sets discards the session instead of writing an empty workout.

features.title: Close the app mid-workout and pick up where you left off
steps: Launch with -uitest-persist -uitest-reset, start Day 1 and log two sets.
Terminate and relaunch with -uitest-persist. The Workout screen shows Resume in place of the black card.
Tap Resume. The logger opens on the same exercise with both sets logged.
A session idle for more than 3 hours (a configurable default) closes itself at launch, ending at its last set.

features.title: See this week's workouts, Monday to Sunday, and open a past session
steps: Launch with -uitest-scenario workout-history. On Workout, tap History.
Weeks run Monday to Sunday, newest first, each with its sessions and working-set count. Weeks without sessions show no 0 rows.
Tap a session: its exercises and sets as weight x reps. Tap an exercise: its past sessions, newest first.
features.tap_budget: 1 tap to History; 1 tap per drill-down

features.title: Import a workout program from a JSON file in the Files app
steps: On Workout, tap Import program. The Files picker opens for a .json file; in -uitest a fixture picker returns a synthetic program.
The file uses the bundled seed's format. A valid file adds its templates (replacing earlier imports with the same key), leaves history alone, and shows how many templates were imported.
An invalid file shows what is wrong and changes nothing.
This is how Isaac's own program reaches the phone. It never enters the repo; the fixture is generic (D-034).

features.title: Tap Food and land straight in the camera, with Home at the top left and a Photo/Barcode switch
steps: Tap the Food card. The camera opens at once, full screen (in -uitest the fixture photo source shows a synthetic plate). Home button at the top left, a Photo/Barcode pill switch, the shutter and a History button.
The first time, iOS asks for the camera (NSCameraUsageDescription). If denied, the screen says how to turn it on in Settings.
Tap the shutter. The photo is saved to local storage as a captured meal before any network call, and a sheet shows "Matching...".
features.tap_budget: 1 tap from Home to the camera; 1 tap for the shutter

features.title: Take a photo and see its items matched against every dining hall's menu for that meal
steps: Tap the shutter. The app sends the downscaled photo, its hash, a client meal id and the meal period to the VM server (POST /scan, server/README.md), which matches it against the menus of all dining halls open for that meal (D-035).
A sheet lists the matched items, each with its hall, servings, and kcal and protein as low-high ranges, plus meal totals as ranges. Never a single number.
An item not on any menu comes back as a rough estimate with a wider range and a "rough" badge.
In -uitest the fake transport answers with a synthetic fixture.

features.title: Search dining items, restaurants and packaged food from the camera screen
steps: On the camera screen, tap the search bar and type. Results from the VM (GET /search) come grouped: dining hall items (with the hall), restaurants, packaged food.
Tap a result. The item list opens with that item at 1 serving and its ranges.
With no good match, tap "Estimate from text". The VM (GET /search with estimate=true) returns a rough estimate, shown with the "rough" badge and a wider range.
In -uitest the fake transport answers search and text estimate with synthetic fixtures.
features.tap_budget: 1 tap into search, typing, 1 tap to pick

features.title: Fix the item list (replace, remove, half servings, add) and log the meal with one Log tap
steps: After a photo (fixture match), tap an item's name. Search opens; pick a replacement. The item and the totals update.
Tap - or + on an item: servings change in half steps, never below 0.5, and the ranges recompute.
Remove an item: it leaves the list and the totals.
Tap + Add item, search and pick: it joins the list at 1 serving.
Tap Log, the single Log button. The meal is saved as confirmed, the sheet closes to the camera, and an undo toast shows.
features.tap_budget: 1 tap (Log) when nothing needs fixing; 1-2 taps per fix

features.title: Switch to Barcode, scan a package, and get it from Open Food Facts
steps: On the camera, switch the pill to Barcode. VisionKit's DataScanner reads the code; in -uitest a fixture barcode source returns a synthetic code.
The code goes to the VM (GET /barcode/{gtin}), which looks it up in Open Food Facts. The item list opens with the product, its serving label and ranges, ready to Log.
An unknown code shows "Not found" and offers search instead.

features.title: Photograph a meal offline; it waits in a queue and gets matched once the server is back
steps: Launch with -uitest-offline -uitest-persist -uitest-reset and tap the shutter. The meal is saved and shows "Pending, will match when online"; today shows "+1 pending", never 0 kcal.
Relaunch online with -uitest-persist. The queue retries in order, the meal gets its items and ranges, and it is ready to Log.
Nothing pending is ever deleted automatically.

features.title: A logged meal is written to Apple Health as one food entry
steps: Log a meal (fixture match). It is saved locally first, then written through HealthStore as one HKCorrelation of type food holding dietary energy and protein: the midpoints, with low and high in metadata, and the meal id as the sync identifier.
The meal shows "In Health". If the write is denied (the fake can deny), it shows "Not in Health" and the meal is kept.

features.title: See today's food as ranges with no target, and fix or delete a past meal in history
steps: Launch with -uitest-scenario food-history. The camera's top strip shows today's kcal and protein as summed low-high ranges and the meal count. No target, ring or "remaining". Nothing logged shows "--".
Tap History. Days newest first with day totals as ranges; each meal with a thumbnail, items, ranges and source; pending meals pinned at the top of their day.
Tap a meal. The same item editor opens; change a serving and Save. The meal and the totals update, and its Health entry is replaced.
Tap Delete. The meal leaves the list and the totals, and its Health entry is deleted.
features.tap_budget: 0 taps for today's totals; 1 tap to History; 1 tap per edit

features.title: Open Data for the first time and connect Apple Health with one sheet, then check sources and permissions
steps: Tap the Data card the first time. An empty state says what Stezu reads and writes and why, with one Connect Apple Health button. Nothing is asked at app launch.

Tap Connect. HealthStore.requestAuthorization shows one system sheet for every v1 type (the fake records it in -uitest). Afterwards Data opens straight to the overview, and the empty state does not return.

From the overview, tap Sources. One row per Health type: present or "--", last sample date, source apps and sample count over the last 7 days, the hint for denied reads (Health app, profile, Apps, Stezu), and a "Not in Health" list of failed writes.
features.tap_budget: 1 tap to connect, once; 1 tap to Sources

features.title: See this week's weight trend and weigh in with one tap
steps: Launch with -uitest-scenario data-week (synthetic samples in the fake HealthStore). Data shows this week, Monday to Sunday. The Weight row: trend weight, the trend's change this week, weigh-ins as coverage ("5 of 7") and the confidence reason.
Tap Weigh in. A stepper prefilled with the last weigh-in, in 0.1 lb steps, with no keyboard. Tap Save: one body-mass sample is written through HealthStore and the row updates.
A week with no weigh-ins shows "--".
features.tap_budget: 0 taps to see the week; 1 tap plus Save to weigh in

features.title: See this week's steps, sleep, HRV and resting heart rate, each with its coverage
steps: Launch with -uitest-scenario data-week. Rows: Steps (mean per day, "6 of 7"), Sleep (mean time asleep, nights "5 of 7", labelled "context"), HRV (median ms and sample count, labelled "context"), Resting HR (mean, days with a value).
Steps come from a statistics query so Health merges sources; sleep nights are built from sleepAnalysis samples.
Any metric without data this week shows "--" with its coverage, never 0.

features.title: See this week's food intake ranges and workouts on Data
steps: Launch with a scenario holding synthetic meals and sessions. The Food row shows the weekly mean kcal and protein over logged days as ranges, and "logged 5 of 7 days".
The Workouts row shows this week's sessions, merging Stezu sessions with Health workouts, each marked by source.
No meals or no workouts this week show "--".

features.title: Tap a metric to see its last 8 weeks, then tap a week to see its days
steps: On the overview, tap any row. One detail template for every metric: 8 weekly values with their coverage, and the source and evidence note at the bottom. Weight also shows weigh-in dots and the trend line.
Tap a week: its days, Monday to Sunday; days without data show "--".
features.tap_budget: 1 tap into a metric; 1 tap into a week

features.title: Open a day and see everything recorded on it
steps: From a week in metric detail, tap a day. The Day view lists everything on that date: weigh-in, meals with ranges, workouts with sets, the sleep night, HRV, steps. Each record shows its source.
Stezu's own records can be edited or deleted from here; Health records are read-only.

features.title: See today's food, this week's workouts and the trend weight on the Home cards with 0 taps
steps: Launch with a scenario holding synthetic meals, sessions and weigh-ins.

Home cards: Data shows the trend weight and weigh-ins this week ("5 of 7"); Food shows today's kcal and protein ranges and the meal count; Workout shows sessions this week and the next template. No target anywhere (D-032).
Without data each card shows "--", never 0.

features.title: See this week's blood oxygen, respiratory rate and temperature from the strap, each with its coverage
steps: Launch with -uitest-scenario data-week. Below the S-022 rows, three more rows, each labelled "context": Blood oxygen (weekly median %, readings count), Respiratory rate (weekly median breaths/min, nights with data), Temperature (weekly median, nights with data).
Add read access for oxygenSaturation, respiratoryRate and bodyTemperature (plus appleSleepingWristTemperature if present) to the HealthKit read set, so the one Connect sheet from S-020 covers them.
Sources lists each new type with its source app and sample count.
A metric with no samples this week shows "--" with its coverage, never 0.

features.title: Your Apple Health data and logged workouts copy themselves to Hermes on the VM, and Settings shows when the last sync ran
steps: After Apple Health is connected (S-020), the app sends every type it reads, plus Stezu's own logged workouts and sets, to POST /sync on the VM server through VMTransport. The contract is in server/README.md.

The first sync backfills the last 90 days. After that it sends only what is new, using HKAnchoredObjectQuery anchors persisted on the device, and sends deletions too. Requests are batched (about 2,000 samples each) and idempotent: every sample carries its HealthKit UUID, every Stezu record its own id.
Sync runs when the app opens or comes to the foreground, and after a workout is finished. It never blocks the UI. With no server or no network, it waits and retries later; nothing is lost.
Settings shows a Hermes sync row: last sync time and sample count, or "--" before the first sync, plus a Sync now button (1 tap).
Launch with -uitest-scenario sync. FakeVMTransport records the batches. The UI test opens Settings, taps Sync now, and sees the row update with the fake's counts.

features.title: Logged meals copy themselves to Hermes too, with their items, ranges and sources
steps: Every confirmed or edited meal goes to POST /sync as a meal record: the id, eaten-at time, day key, items with ranges and source, and the confirm state. Deleted meals are sent as tombstones. Photos are not sent again; the server already has the photos it scanned.
Uses the same queue and retry as S-028. Settings' sync count includes meals.
Launch with -uitest-scenario sync-meals. Log a meal; the UI test sees the fake transport receive one meal record and the Settings row count go up.

features.title: Every logged set and finished workout is saved on the phone first, then sent to Hermes as records
steps: Logging a set still saves it on the phone the moment it is logged (D-045). Right after that local save, the app queues one `set` record on the same sync queue as meals (HealthSync.enqueue, D-075). The payload: set id, session id, template key, exercise key and name, pounds (null for bodyweight, never 0), reps, logged-at, and kind (working). Undo queues the same set id with deleted: true.

Finish saves the session on the phone first (D-056), then queues one `workout_session` record: session id, template key and name, start, end, and its exercises with their sets. The Apple Health write stays, but it comes after the local save and never gates the record.
Swaps and custom exercises are part of the session payload (exercise key plus display name), so the server can tell what was actually done.

On the first launch with this build, every session already in finished-workouts.json, and the sets of an unfinished logger, is queued once as records (a backfill). A flag records that the backfill ran, so it never runs twice. Replays are safe because the server keys records by (kind, id) and keeps the newer updated_at.
updated_at has millisecond resolution, so a set logged and undone within a second is still two distinct versions.

Launch with -uitest-scenario sync. Start Day 1, log a set, undo it, log it again, then Finish. FakeVMTransport receives set records (including one deletion) and one workout_session record. Settings' records count goes up.

features.title: A weigh-in is saved on the phone first, then written to Apple Health and sent to Hermes
steps: The one-tap weigh-in now writes to a local weigh-in store on the phone first (weigh-ins.json: id, measured-at, pounds). This store is the app's source of truth for weigh-ins, which reverses D-057's 'Health only'. Then it writes the body-mass sample to Apple Health, tagged with the weigh-in id in metadata, and records whether Health took it. Then it queues a `weigh_in` record (id, measured-at, pounds, inHealth) on the sync queue.
A denied or failed Health write never loses the weigh-in: it stays local, is synced to the VM, and shows 'Not in Health' on Sources.
The weight row, the 8-week detail, Home and the Day view read weigh-ins from the local store. Other apps' body-mass samples (Zepp's profile weight) are never mixed in (D-047).

Migration, once per install: Stezu-sourced body-mass samples already in Health (written by earlier builds) are imported into the local store, matched by Health UUID so nothing is doubled, and then queued as records.
Deleting a weigh-in in the Day view removes it locally first, then from Health by its id, then queues the record with deleted: true.
Launch with -uitest-scenario sync. Weigh in once; FakeVMTransport receives one weigh_in record, the weight row shows it, and deleting it in the Day view sends a deleted record.

features.title: Places you go are recorded in the background, saved on the phone first, and sent to Hermes
steps: Sources gains a Location row. Tapping Allow asks for When In Use and then Always access, the standard two-step iOS flow. The row shows the current permission (Always, While Using, Off) and the time of the last recorded location, or "--".

With Always access, the app monitors visits (CLLocationManager.startMonitoringVisits) and significant location changes (startMonitoringSignificantLocationChanges). Both work in the background and relaunch the app after it is terminated. No continuous GPS, so the battery cost stays low.

Every visit (arrival, departure, latitude, longitude, horizontal accuracy) and every significant change (time, latitude, longitude, accuracy, speed if known) is appended to a local store on the phone first (D-076). Then it is queued on the existing sync queue as a `visit` or `location` record. A visit whose departure is not known yet is updated, not duplicated, when the departure arrives. Use the record field names documented in server/README.md.
When an event wakes the app in the background, it saves the event and tries one sync pass within the time iOS allows. Anything not sent stays queued; nothing is dropped.
Data shows a Places row for this week: the number of visits recorded and the days with location data ("5 of 7"), or "--". No map, no inferred places in v1.

Launch with -uitest-scenario location. A fake location source delivers two visits and one significant change. Sources shows Location as Always with a last-fix time, the Places row shows 2 visits, and FakeVMTransport receives the records.

features.title: Health data and queued records reach Hermes in the background, even on days you don't open the app
steps: Register a BGAppRefreshTask with the identifier listed in the Info.plist key BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers. Schedule it after every sync pass and at launch (earliest begin about 1 hour). iOS decides when it actually runs.

When it runs: read Health changes since the saved anchors (the same anchored pass as S-028, D-067), then send queued batches, within about 25 seconds, and stop cleanly when iOS calls the expiration handler. Anchors only move after a batch is saved to the queue, so an interrupted run loses nothing.
Health data is only readable while the phone is unlocked. A run while it is locked reads nothing and still sends the queue (records, visits).
Settings shows the last background sync time next to the last foreground sync, or "--".
Launch with -uitest-scenario background-sync and trigger the handler through a debug hook. FakeVMTransport receives a batch, and Settings shows a background sync time.

features.title: Importing a program file replaces the whole program, and workout history is kept
steps: After a valid file is picked, a confirmation shows the file's template names: "Replace your program with Push, Pull? Your workout history is kept." with Replace and Cancel. Cancel changes nothing.

Replace leaves the template list holding exactly the file's templates, in the file's order. Templates the file lacks are removed from the list. This reverses D-052's upsert-only import, as its Reverse-if allows.
History is kept. Finished sessions of removed templates stay in History under their own names, and their records on the server are untouched (no deletions are queued).
An unfinished workout started from a removed template can still be logged and finished. Its logger keeps its own copy of the exercises (D-046).

The bundled seed never brings removed templates back. Once a program has been imported, the library records it (a `programImported` flag that decodes as false from older files), and later seed upserts are skipped.
An invalid file still leaves the library exactly as it was, with the same messages as before (D-052).

Launch with -uitest, open Workout and import the generic two-template fixture over the default seed, which has more templates. The confirmation names both, and Replace leaves exactly those two in file order. A finished session from a removed template is still listed in History.
features.tap_budget: Import, pick the file, Replace (1 more tap than before)

features.title: An optional add-on block (like Abs) can be added to the end of any workout with one tap
steps: A template in a program file may carry "addOn": true. Add-ons pass the same validation as other templates. Library files from older builds decode with no add-ons. Add-ons are not listed as days on the Workout screen.

While any workout is running, the logger shows one button per add-on below the day's exercises, named after it ("+ Abs"). Tapping it appends the add-on's exercises to the current workout, after the day's own, and the button goes away. The appended exercises behave like any other: logging, undo, swap, and the rest timer with each exercise's rest.

It stays one workout: one Finish, one Apple Health workout, one workout_session record. The session keeps the day's template key and lists the add-on's exercises with their sets. Set records carry the add-on exercise keys. An appended exercise with no logged sets is left out of the saved session.
Last numbers for an add-on exercise come from the most recent session that had that exercise key, whatever its template, because add-ons follow different days. This extends D-046 for add-ons only.
Quitting and relaunching mid-workout keeps the appended exercises and their sets (the logger's saved state includes them).

Launch with -uitest and import a generic fixture with two days and one add-on. The Workout screen lists only the two days. Start a day, tap the add-on button, log one set of its first exercise, and Finish. History shows one session containing the add-on exercise.

features.title: Next workout follows the last one you did; any day can be started off schedule, and today's finished workout can be continued
steps: Bug: Home and Workout both call TemplateLibrary.next(after: nil), so Next is always the first day. Next is now the day after the template of the most recently finished Stezu session (by end time), whatever day it was, including one started off schedule. Rotation is by order, never by date or weekday. With no finished session, or the last template no longer in the program, Next is the first day.
Home's Workout card subtitle and the Workout screen's black card show the same Next, computed by one StezuCore function from the library and finished sessions.

Off schedule: the Workout screen lists every other day below the black card with its own Start, plus Empty workout (these exist; keep them reachable in one tap). Starting one doesn't change the program; it moves Next to the day after it once finished.

Continue: a finished session that started less than 12 hours ago shows Continue in History's session view and on the Workout screen ("Continue Push, 4 sets" as a row under the black card). Continue reopens the logger on that session: same session id, its logged sets shown, and new sets append. Older sessions show no Continue.

Finishing a continued session saves it under the same id (replacing, not duplicating, in History). It replaces its Apple Health workout: delete the old one this app wrote, matched by the session id in metadata, then save a new one from the first to the last set. It re-sends the workout_session record with the same id and a newer updated_at. New sets go out as set records as usual.
A workout in progress still shows Resume in place of the black card (S-009). Continue is only for finished sessions.

Launch with -uitest and a fixture whose last finished session is day 1. The black card and Home say day 2. Start day 3 off schedule, log a set and Finish; Next becomes the day after day 3. Continue that session, log one more set, Finish; History shows one session with both sets.

features.title: One TopBar on every area screen and sheet: Home on the left, one text action on the right, the title beneath
steps: Build TopBar per design/system/components/TopBar/README.md. Home is a 44 pt `house` symbol in ink with no fill; on the camera it sits on a surface disc. The right slot holds one text button in t-headline ("Finish", "Sources", "Done"). The screen title sits beneath, in t-title-1, and says what the screen holds now ("This week", "Resting HR", "Tue, Oct 21").

Sheets show a drag indicator and a TopBar with Done, or the rung above it, on the right. Sheets have no toolbar items: iOS 26 draws those as floating glass pills, which caused the shadowed Done Isaac flagged.

Use TopBar on every area screen and every sheet (find them all: `.sheet`, `.fullScreenCover`, `NavigationStack` titles). Keep each control's accessibility id (nav.home, screen.<area>.title, each Done).
Swipe down still closes every sheet, except where a sheet blocks it on purpose because of unsaved edits.

UI test: open each sheet in turn. Assert its Done is hittable at the top right (frame maxX within 40 pt of the screen width) and closes the sheet, and that every area screen shows nav.home at the top left.

features.title: Chart components (Sparkline, WeekBars, CoverageDots, WeightChart) and the metric detail screen for every Data metric
steps: Build reusable SwiftUI views per design/system/components: Sparkline (72 x 28), WeekBars, CoverageDots and WeightChart. Port WeightChart from the Canvas version to Swift Charts. Use only Swift Charts, a system framework. Every chart has an accessibilityChartDescriptor.
Sparkline: Monday to Sunday. Lines for levels, bars for counts. A missing day is a dashed track slot, never zero. Today is at full strength with a dot; older days step back.

WeekBars: 8 weekly bars, oldest on the left, each labelled with its week and coverage. The current week is at full strength and past weeks at 55%. An estimate (food) is a band from low to high with a 3 px midpoint. A week without data is a dashed slot with "--" above it. Two light gridlines, no y-axis numbers.

Colours: data-energy for kcal, data-protein for protein, data-heart for heart rate and resting HR, and ink for steps, sets and weight. Raw dots use data-sample. Energy and protein are never in one plot.

The metric detail screen (MetricDetailView): TopBar, then a WeekBars well (140 tall on surface), the weeks list, and finally sources and method. Tapping a bar does the same as tapping its row, which opens that week's days. Every This week metric uses it: weight, steps, workouts (working sets), food (energy and protein as two panels), HRV, resting HR and breathing. Sleep is excluded, because S-040 builds its own screen.
Launch with -uitest and generic fixtures. Open Steps: 8 bars, one of them a dashed absent week showing "--". Open Food: two separate panels. Each chart has an accessibility label.

features.title: Home cards follow GlanceCard: last night's sleep on Data, today's food, and this week's sessions with day dots
steps: Build Home per design/system/components/GlanceCard/README.md and walkthroughs/home.html. Each card has three rows. Row 1: the area name (15 medium, ink) with its time frame ("Last night", "Today", "This week") in t-label/muted. Row 2: one number centred in t-big, shrinking to fit the width, with a small unit beside it and a small picture on the right where listed below. Row 3: a detail row with one fact on the left and one on the right, 13 pt muted with the value in ink.

The three cards share the height evenly, and Home never scrolls. Each whole card is the button: remove any button or pill inside a card. Tapping Data opens This week, Food opens the camera, and Workout opens the Workout screen. Keep the ids home.card.<area>. Each card is one VoiceOver element ("Data, Last night, 7 hours 12 minutes asleep").

Data: last night's time asleep, from the same SleepNights code as the Data screen's Sleep row. On the right, the 7 nights as small bars, using the Sparkline from S-042. Detail row: "Usual Xh Ym" (the median of up to 30 recorded nights) on the left, and the week's trend weight in lb on the right (D-097). Anything missing shows "--", never 0.
Food: today's kcal range with an en dash. Detail row: the protein range on the left and the meal count on the right.

Workout: the number of sessions this week, with Monday to Sunday CoverageDots on the right (filled means trained, outlined means today). Detail row: "Next: <template>" on the left, from the S-036 rotation, and this week's working sets on the right.
One card is invert, chosen by time of day as now. While a workout is in progress, the Workout card is invert instead.

Launch with -uitest and the sleep and workout fixtures, which are generic. The Data card shows the fixture's time asleep, usual and weight; the Workout card shows its dots and the next template. Tapping anywhere on the Food card opens the camera. With the empty scenario, every number is "--".
features.tap_budget: 0 taps to read; 1 tap per card

features.title: This week follows the walkthrough: grouped cards, a sparkline on every row, whole-row taps, and no blood oxygen or temperature
steps:
Build This week per design/system/walkthroughs/data.html and components/MetricRow/README.md. The cards have headers, in this order:
    1. Body and activity: Weight, Steps.
    2. Food and training: Food, as a kcal range in data-energy; Workouts, showing working sets.
    3. Recovery, with ONE "context only" tag in the card header: Sleep, HRV, Resting HR, Breathing.
    4. Places: the value is this week's visits, with coverage in the subtitle.
  Sources becomes a quiet row at the bottom, not a full-width button.
Remove the Blood oxygen and Temperature rows. This is Isaac's call (D-093), and it overrides the order list in MetricRow's README. Their Health reads and /sync stay as they are.

Each row is a MetricRow: title and coverage, a 72 x 28 Sparkline (S-042), the value in t-value, and a chevron. The WHOLE row is the button, at least 44 pt tall. It opens that metric's detail (the S-042 template). Sleep opens its existing detail until S-040 replaces it.

Sparklines run Monday to Sunday. Levels are lines (weight, HRV, resting HR, breathing); counts are bars (steps, food, workouts, places, sleep). The line is lighter, and only today gets a dot. A missing day is a dashed slot, never a near-zero tick. A rest day in Workouts is a real 0, drawn as a baseline stub.

Launch with -uitest and the strap fixture. There are no Blood oxygen or Temperature rows. Every row has data.spark.<row id>. A fixture day without sleep shows a dashed slot. Tapping the middle of the Steps row opens its detail.
features.tap_budget: 1 tap from Home; 1 more per metric

features.title: Tapping Sleep opens the Sleep screen: last night, a 14-night window, the stages of the night you pick, and one overnight line
steps: Build Sleep per design/system/walkthroughs/data.html (the Sleep screen) and components/Hypnogram/README.md. It is pushed from the Sleep row with the TopBar. The order is: last night's number, the pattern across nights, then the stages of the night you picked.
Top: "Last night", the time asleep, and "Usual Xh Ym, your median of N nights" (up to 30). Descriptive only, with no score, target or colour judgement (D-032).

The window chart is fixed at 14 nights, with no range switch. It draws one bar per night from bedtime to final wake on a shared clock axis. The bedtime and wake usual lines carry their own labels at the top. A night without data is "--". The selected night is full strength and the others step back. Tapping a night selects it, and everything below switches to that night.

Stages of the selected night: a hypnogram with Awake, REM, Core and Deep lanes in the sleep-* colours, with each stage's total written on its lane (no separate legend). "Estimated by the strap" sits next to the chart. Wake-ups are the warmest mark, and the count is written under the chart: "2 wake-ups, 6m awake after falling asleep" or "No wake-ups after falling asleep". Unspecified asleep counts as Core.
One overnight line of three numbers: heart rate low–high in bpm (data-heart), breathing in br/min, and HRV in ms. These cover the asleep intervals only. There are no range charts.

A "<Weekday, Mon d> as a day" row opens the Day view for the wake date. The footer reads: "Nights are named by the morning you woke up. Tracking only: no score, no target." Nights are named by wake day everywhere.

Reuse SleepNights, the same code used by the Data row and the Home card. Launch with -uitest and a generic multi-night fixture. There are 14 window bars, and the missing night shows "--". Tapping an earlier night changes the top number and the wake-up count.

features.title: The Day view opens with a summary and a folding timeline: places by name, sleep, meals and the workout
steps: Build Day per design/system/walkthroughs/data.html (the Day screen) and components/DayTimeline/README.md, above the existing record list, which keeps Edit and Delete (S-025).

The title is the date, with previous and next day arrows beside it (1 tap per day). Under it is a summary of the day's totals: time asleep, the kcal and protein ranges, the workout, steps and visits. There is no steps lane.

Place names are resolved on the phone with CLGeocoder's reverse geocoding and cached on the device by visit id. Names never leave the phone: they are not added to /sync records, logs or screenshots (D-098). Without a name, the visit shows its times.
Tapping sleep opens that night on the Sleep screen. Tapping a meal or the workout scrolls the list below to its row. Nothing is invented: an empty day is an empty timeline, never placeholders.

Launch with -uitest and a generic fixture day: a night, two meals, one workout and two visits, with fake place names injected through a fake geocoder. The timeline shows each, the empty hours are folded, the arrows move a day, and tapping a meal scrolls to its row.
features.tap_budget: 0 taps (top of the Day view); 1 per day with the arrows

features.title: Food follows the walkthrough: today's total on the camera, a match sheet with half-step servings, and a Food Today screen
steps: Build per design/system/walkthroughs/food.html and the Shutter, SegmentedPill, MealItem, RangeValue and UndoToast READMEs.

Camera: today's running total is a strip at the top on camera-scrim. Search and History sit beside it, the shutter (74 pt) and Photo/Barcode below. Home sits on a surface disc. Every piece of text sits on a scrim or a solid surface, so none is drawn bare over the preview.

Match sheet, opened by the shutter: totals first (energy and protein ranges, each in its data colour, separately), then the items. Each item has - and + buttons that change servings in half steps (minimum 0.5), and the totals update live. "Add item" opens search. Log is full width at the bottom of the sheet.

History opens Food Today. It has energy and protein ranges large in their data colours; then each meal with its photo, time, items and ranges (tapping one keeps the existing edit and delete, S-019); then This week, drawn as a low-to-high band per day. The missing day is a dashed slot, and today says "so far".
Launch with -uitest and generic fixtures. Shoot, raise one item to 1.5 servings and check that the totals change, then Log. Food Today lists the meal, and its week shows a band for today.
features.tap_budget: 3 taps to log a meal (Food card, shutter, Log)

features.title: Workout follows the walkthrough: the next template as the black card, an inline rest in the logger, and a summary after Finish
steps: Build per design/system/walkthroughs/workout.html and the SetLogger, RestTimer, SetRow, Stepper and CoverageDots READMEs.

Workout screen:
    - The black card is the next template (S-036), listing its exercises, with a full-width Start.
    - This week uses the same day dots as Home and shows the session and working-set counts.
    - Every other day shows when it was last done ("Pull, 3 days ago") and has a one-tap Start.
    - The Continue row (S-036) and Import program stay.

Logger (the black card):
    - The exercise name in t-title-2 and "Set 2 of 2".
    - The rep range and "Last 135 x 8, 7d ago".
    - The steppers.
    - Log, full width at the bottom of the card, never moving. BW is an outline pill to its left.
    - After Log, the rest countdown, using the exercise's rest, appears INSIDE the card above the steppers, with -15, +15 and Skip. The Live Activity is unchanged.
    - The ellipsis menu holds Swap and Skip exercise.

Under the card:
    - The next set as a dashed row with last time's numbers (what to beat, not a target).
    - Logged sets, newest first.
    - A thin progress bar of segments across exercises, with the next exercise named.
    - The add-on buttons (+ Abs, S-035).
  The area nav is hidden while logging. Finish is at the top right.

Finish opens a summary:
    - Duration, working sets, volume (lb x reps, bodyweight excluded) and In Health or Not in Health.
    - Each exercise's sets, then its best set compared with the last session of the same template ("+5 lb", "same", "-1 rep"), in plain ink, with no green or red.
    - Undo for 8 seconds reopens the session; Finish stays one tap.
    - Done returns to Workout.

Launch with -uitest and generic fixtures. Start the next template, log a set (the rest appears inside the card and Log doesn't move), Skip the rest, Finish. The summary shows the comparison with the fixture's last session, and Undo reopens the session.
